target_customer: Fashion shoppers in dense cities, later luxury shoppers in New York, ordering from nearby boutiques; retail partners pay commission
problem: Shoppers want to try clothes before buying and return instantly; Ole delivered items from local stores, waited while the customer tried them on and took back what they did not keep.
business_model: Marketplace with a 25 percent commission from retail partners plus a delivery fee of about 5 dollars (TechCrunch, Nov 2023)
product_category: on-demand fashion delivery and try-at-home marketplace

founders.name: Alon Hendelman
previous_startups: Engie (co-founder; connected-car app and marketplace; YC page says he was on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list for it)

founders.name: Gal Aharon
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him a longtime friend of Hendelman.

founders.name: Omer Hendelman
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Nov 2023) lists him as COO and former VP of operations at Avo; Modern Retail calls him Hendelman's cousin and part of the founding team. Not listed on the YC page; role as co-founder not stated by the company's own page.

competitors.name: ThredUP Goody Boxes
competitors.what: Try-before-you-buy clothing boxes shipped to the home, a Stitch Fix style alternative

competitors.name: Jetblack (Walmart)
competitors.what: Text based personal shopping and delivery in New York; shut down in February 2020, so it was a failed precedent rather than an active rival in 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app with store inventory feeds and driver dispatch is standard engineering; the hard parts are logistics density and partner integrations, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Courier plus store inventory model could be copied by food delivery and luxury retailers; partner relationships were the main asset.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Ole; Modern Retail (Dec 2023) names food delivery players and Need It For Tonight as nearby rivals.

market_need_then: The YC page reported 35 thousand dollars monthly GMV growing 35 percent per month with an average order near 200 dollars versus about 30 for typical on-demand. By 2023 in New York the company reported 450 dollar average orders and 40 percent repeat customers.

branding.domain_note: Uses oleshop.com, not ole.com (the YC page lists oleshop.com, now returning 404).

identity.visual_style: Luxury positioning in New York with partners such as Miu Miu and Acne Studios
identity.voice_and_tone: Premium, speed focused: delivery in 50 minutes

branding.brand_signature: The promise of delivery in 50 minutes with a courier who waits while you try on
branding.community_and_virality: Fashion and tech press coverage: WWD (Sep 2022), Vogue Business (Dec 2022), TechCrunch (Nov 2023), Modern Retail (Dec 2023) per the YC page and opened articles.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage by WWD, Vogue Business, TechCrunch and Modern Retail and luxury partner names suggest a solid niche brand, but there is no evidence of community or merch, and the name collides with many other Ole names.

pivots.from: Mass market fashion delivery in Tel Aviv from nearby stores
pivots.to: Luxury fashion delivery in New York with 50 minute guarantee
pivots.why: Tel Aviv operations were discontinued in early summer 2023 and New York became the main market (Modern Retail); the company's stated reason is not given

outcome_analysis: Ole launched in Tel Aviv in 2022, closed it in summer 2023 and moved to luxury delivery in New York, raising 1.5 million dollars in November 2023 on top of 500 thousand from YC. Reported traction included 450 dollar order values and 40 percent repeat use. YC lists the company as inactive, but no shutdown, acquisition or layoff report was found after December 2023, so the cause is not public. The on-demand delivery category is capital intensive, but no source ties that to Ole's end.
notes: Rounds come from TechCrunch (Nov 2023), which does not label the stage; VCBacked and FundedIQ say 1.5M seed in Nov 2023 with a slightly different investor list (VCBacked lists Michael Shor; TechCrunch lists Light Ray Ventures); TechCrunch is used. Total raised 2M matches the rounds. YC check date for the 500K is 2022 per TechCrunch. Company site oleshop.com returned 404. No competitor source dated near the Jan 2022 batch describing active direct rivals was found; Need It For Tonight and others appear only in late 2023 articles and are not listed. Jetblack is a failed precedent, not an active rival. Omer Hendelman is recorded as a founding team member by TechCrunch and Modern Retail, not by the YC page.
